chunks: Say: 'Should we call in place of God one who can neither help nor do us harm, and turn back after having been guided by God, like a man beguiled by the devils who wanders perplexed in the wilderness while his friends call him back to the right path, saying: 'Come to us, this way?' Say: "God's guidance is (true) guidance, and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of all the worlds."
ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor used in the Quran to describe those who worship idols after knowing the truth?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to highlight the logical coherence of Tawhid, contrasting the absurdity of returning to ignorance (Jahiliyyah) with the clarity of divine guidance. The metaphor of being 'led astray by devils' underscores the internal and external forces that cause believers to waver, while the command to 'submit' emphasizes the active, conscious choice of the heart in accepting Islam. This passage serves as a foundational argument for the necessity of following the Ahl al-Bayt as the true interpreters of this divine guidance.
